$comment: One row per bag per publication. These are THEIR claims and THEIR words, never merged into our bag records. 'claimed' is what the outlet printed; our measurements live in data/bags/. Conflicts are derived from this file, not authored.

mentions.praise: Compression straps fit a 4-day load without the expander; dent-proof in the bat test.
mentions.caveat: May be too large for some overhead bins.

mentions.praise: Front-access pocket, removable garment sleeve, compression straps.
mentions.caveat: Heaviest pick at 10.7 lb.

mentions.praise: Lightest pick; Roxkin shell bounces back into shape.
mentions.caveat: Expands only 0.5 in; minimal organization.

mentions.praise: Smooth wheels even on carpet; stayed clean over 6 months.
mentions.caveat: Limited capacity — best for light packers.

mentions.praise: Strong capacity for the price; scratches buffed out by hand.
mentions.caveat: Wobbly telescoping handle; no TSA lock.

mentions.praise: 2.25 in of expansion, more than typical; minimal damage in drop and bat tests.
mentions.caveat: Some international airlines may force a check when fully expanded.

mentions.praise: Ships with compression cubes, shoe bags, laundry bag; external laptop sleeve.
mentions.caveat: 23-in height risks a forced check on smaller airlines.

mentions.praise: Zipperless build makes it impossible to overpack past international limits.
mentions.caveat: No expansion; ~8.8 lb empty.

mentions.praise: Largest capacity tested (50 to 62 L); 20 handle heights.
mentions.caveat: Cumbersome in tight corners when full; may be gate-checked.

mentions.praise: Minimalist and easy to pack; only 5.5 lb.
mentions.caveat: Smallest capacity on the list; 2 fixed wheels, not 360.

mentions.praise: Among the smoothest wheels; 12 handle heights.
mentions.caveat: No expansion zipper — caps it at a 2-3 day trip.

mentions.praise: Lightest full-size pick; resisted dents under the bat test.
mentions.caveat: No interior compartments; picked up cosmetic scratches.

mentions.praise: Smallest wheeled bag on the list; fits under most seats.
mentions.caveat: Interior lining doesn't feel durable.

mentions.praise: Removable compression cube; big wheels work on 2 or 4.
mentions.caveat: Front pocket lacks padding — a laptop screen broke in T+L's table-drop test.

mentions.praise: Armor-like textured shell, corner guards, USB port, 4 interior zip compartments.
mentions.caveat: Not expandable.

mentions.praise: Spacious for its compact footprint; zero wear after drop and bat tests.
mentions.caveat: Would benefit from more interior pockets.

mentions.praise: Latch closure means it can't be overstuffed — a plus for tight bins.
mentions.caveat: Heaviest pick at 10.5 lb; aluminum dents and scratches easily.

mentions.praise: Tegris shell survived a table drop with only bumper scuffing.
mentions.caveat: Minimal organization — just one zip pocket.

mentions.praise: Well-padded 17-in laptop pocket; flexible softside squeezes into tight spaces.
mentions.caveat: Flimsy-feeling handle; rolls better on two wheels than four.

mentions.praise: 40 L in a compact, 2.1 lb package; converts to a backpack.
mentions.caveat: Rugged look won't suit everyone.

mentions.praise: Lockable zippers, slashproof fabric, RFID pocket, steel cable anchor.
mentions.caveat: Heavy and bulky for a backpack.

mentions.praise: Best value on the list; smoothest zippers tested; strong interior organization.
mentions.caveat: Wheels stick on carpet.

mentions.praise: Under 5 lb thanks to two wheels; two wheels performed almost like four.
mentions.caveat: No backpack straps.

mentions.praise: Fit every overhead bin across 4 US flights (Delta, Southwest, United); scuffs wipe clean.
mentions.caveat: Telescopic handle sticks between its three heights.

mentions.praise: Latches onto the matching checked roller to pull both at once.
mentions.caveat: Quick turns can detach it from the checked bag.

mentions.praise: Holds more than it looks.
mentions.caveat: Hard to maneuver despite not being heavy.

mentions.praise: Thoughtful organization.
mentions.caveat: Over 9 lb empty eats into strict international weight allowances.

mentions.praise: Spacious expandable interior.
mentions.caveat: 14.2 in wide may exceed some airline limits.

mentions.praise: Separate compartment for dirty shoes.
mentions.caveat: Materials feel less durable; width runs large.

mentions.praise: Designed to the European 55 x 40 x 20 envelope: it trades depth for width rather than maximising a US-shaped box.
